from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The First Derivative", [
            "The derivative represents a slope.",
            "It shows the rate of change.",
            "Velocity is the first derivative."
        ])
        
        # Define function and plot
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * (x - 2)**2 + 1, color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        axes.add(curve)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        dot = Dot(color=RED)
        dot.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 0.25 * (1 - 2)**2 + 1))
        
        tangent = TangentLine(curve, alpha=0.3, length=2, color=WHITE)
        self.add(dot, tangent)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Animate tangent moving
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(dot, curve), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Highlight zero slope point
        zero_slope = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 1), color=GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(zero_slope))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Positive second derivative is concave up.",
            "Negative second derivative is concave down.",
            "Zero indicates an inflection point.",

            "Roller coasters show these curves."
        ]

        label_up = Text("f''(x) > 0", color=BLUE, font_size=24)
        label_down = Text("f''(x) < 0", color=RED, font_size=24)
        inflection_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        label_inflection = Text("f''(x) = 0", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(curve_up, "A2", "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(label_up, "D3")
        self.play(Create(curve_up), Write(label_up))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        self.place_in_area(curve_down, "C2", "E5")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Position changes to velocity.",
            "Velocity changes to acceleration.",
            "Acceleration changes to jerk.",
            "Hierarchy shows higher order derivatives.",
            "Jerk is the third derivative."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Motion Equation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Color codes for lines
        colors = [BLUE_B, GREEN_B, YELLOW_B, ORANGE, RED_B]
        
        # Elements
        s_t = MathTex(r"s(t) \text{ (Position)}").set_color(colors[0])
        v_t = MathTex(r"v(t) = s'(t)").set_color(colors[1])
        a_t = MathTex(r"a(t) = v'(t) = s''(t)").set_color(colors[2])
        j_t = MathTex(r"j(t) = a'(t) = s'''(t)").set_color(colors[3])
        text_jerk = Text("Jerk", font_size=32).set_color(colors[4])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(s_t, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(s_t))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(v_t, 'C2', scale_factor=1.2)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(a_t, 'D2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(a_t))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        self.setup_layout("Summary & Quick Check", [

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

outline.topic: Higher Order Derivatives: From Velocity to Acceleration

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The First Derivative
sections.content: Briefly recall that the first derivative f'(x) represents the rate of change or the slope of the tangent line. Visualize this as a point moving along a curve: f'(x) tracks how fast the position changes.
sections.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: f(t) is the distance covered at time t, f'(t) is the instantaneous velocity.

sections.title: Defining Higher Order Derivatives
sections.content: Introduce the concept of differentiating the derivative. If f'(x) is a function, we can take its derivative again to get f''(x). Graphically, this measures the 'curvature' or how the slope itself is changing over time.
sections.example: If the cheetah's velocity (f'(t)) increases, the 'rate of change of velocity' is the second derivative, f''(t), known as acceleration.

sections.title: Visualizing Concavity
sections.content: Use a graphical animation showing a parabola. When f''(x) > 0, the curve is 'concave up' (like a cup); when f''(x) < 0, it is 'concave down' (like a hill). Explain that f''(x) = 0 often indicates an inflection point.
sections.example: A roller coaster track: The second derivative tells the rider how sharply the track is curving upwards or downwards at any point.

sections.title: Application: The Motion Equation
sections.content: Synthesize the concept by showing the hierarchy of motion: Position (f) → Velocity (f') → Acceleration (f''). Emphasize that higher-order derivatives (f''', etc.) represent 'jerk' (the rate of change of acceleration).
sections.example: A high-speed elevator starting to move: The jerk (f'''(t)) is what you feel as the initial 'tug' or jolt in your stomach.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
sections.content: Consolidate the notation (f'', f''', f^(n)). Remind students that each order of differentiation tells us about the 'rate of change of the previous rate'.
sections.example: Quick poll: If a rocket's position is f(t), what does the 3rd derivative f'''(t) describe? (Answer: The rate of change of acceleration).
